title: 상황 말하고 이어 말하기: 비가 오는데 우산 있어요?
objective: By the end, you can choose -는데, -ㄴ데, -은데, or -인데 for verbs, adjectives, and nouns. You can also say when -는데 and -지만 both work and when only -는데 works.
summary: Learn the connective ending -는데 to give background before a question or request, and to contrast two facts, compared with -지만.

task.title: Practice using -는데
task.line: Change the word in brackets, choose the right ending, or join the sentences. Then check your answers.

forms.when: Action verbs in the present. Words ending in 있다/없다 also take -는데 (맛있다 → 맛있는데). ㄹ drops: 살다 → 사는데.
forms.means: Gives the situation first, then you ask, suggest, or say more.
forms.exampleMeaning: It's raining now. Do you have an umbrella?

forms.when: Adjective stems ending in a vowel: 싸다 → 싼데. ㄹ adjectives drop ㄹ: 길다 → 긴데.
forms.exampleMeaning: This bag is pretty, but it's too expensive.

forms.when: Adjective stems ending in a consonant: 작다 → 작은데. ㅂ adjectives change: 덥다 → 더운데.
forms.means: Contrast or background, the same as the other forms.
forms.exampleMeaning: The room is small, but it's very clean.

forms.when: After a noun (from N + 이다): 학생 → 학생인데, 회사원 → 회사원인데.
forms.means: Introduces who or what someone or something is before you say more.
forms.example: 저는 회사원인데 요즘 저녁에 한국어를 배워요.
forms.exampleMeaning: I'm an office worker, and these days I learn Korean in the evenings.

forms.when: The situation is in the past: 가다 → 갔는데, 먹다 → 먹었는데.
forms.means: Past background. What comes next is often unexpected.
forms.example: 어제 친구 집에 갔는데 친구가 없었어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: I went to my friend's house yesterday, but my friend wasn't there.

forms.when: For contrast, both work. For background before a question, request, or suggestion, use only -는데.
forms.example: 김치는 매운데 맛있어요. / 김치는 맵지만 맛있어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: Kimchi is spicy, but it's tasty.

watchOut: 좋는데 (X) → 좋은데 (O): 좋다 is an adjective, so it takes -은데, not -는데.
맛있은데 (X) → 맛있는데 (O): words ending in 있다/없다 always take -는데.
배고프지만 같이 밥 먹을까요? (X) → 배고픈데 같이 밥 먹을까요? (O): -지만 only shows contrast. To give background before a suggestion, use -는데.
exercises: Write the correct -는데 form of the word in brackets: ① 이 식당은 음식이 (적다) ____ 좀 비싸요. ② 제 동생은 키가 (크다) ____ 저는 작아요. ③ 요즘 날씨가 (춥다) ____ 따뜻한 옷을 입으세요.
Write the correct -는데 form of the word in brackets: ① 저는 부산에 (살다) ____ 서울에 자주 와요. ② 제 친구는 (요리사) ____ 집에서는 요리를 안 해요. ③ 어제 영화를 (보다, past) ____ 재미없었어요.
Choose the right ending. If both are correct, write 'both': ① 지금 마트에 (가는데 / 가지만) 뭐 필요한 거 있어요? ② 한국어는 (어려운데 / 어렵지만) 재미있어요. ③ 이 단어를 (모르는데 / 모르지만) 좀 가르쳐 주세요.
Join the two sentences into one with -는데: ① 내일 친구 생일이에요. 무슨 선물이 좋을까요? ② 그 카페는 커피가 비싸요. 사람이 많아요.

Complete each sentence with -는데 so it fits the situation: ① At a shoe store, the design is cool (멋있다), but the shoes are a bit small: 이 신발은 디자인이 ____ 좀 작아요. ② You are busy (바쁘다) and want a coworker's help: 제가 지금 ____ 이것 좀 도와줄 수 있어요?
answers: ① 적은데 ② 큰데 ③ 추운데
① 사는데 ② 요리사인데 ③ 봤는데
① 가는데 ② both (어려운데 / 어렵지만) ③ 모르는데
① 내일 친구 생일인데 무슨 선물이 좋을까요? ② 그 카페는 커피가 비싼데 사람이 많아요.
